name: Actor_CreateActionTable
summary: Builds the complete action/command table of a field actor: mesh and equip objects, movement controllers, battle action-anim entries, cut/action records and the per-action handler records, then sorts them by priority and registers the default action. No direct caller - the table is installed by the actor class factory.
evidence: 45 callees are now named (Gfx_CreateEquipObjectForNode, Battle_ActionAnimEntry_Create, Actor_Action_CreateMove, Actor_Action_TableEntryCtor, Ui_SceneWindow_Ctor) and the tail call is maybe_Actor_ActionList_SortByPriority; that set only makes sense as an action-table builder, so the first-pass guess is kept. Still no caller, so 'table' vs 'actor setup' cannot be separated.

name: Actor2D_InitFromRecord
signature: void Actor2D_InitFromRecord(Actor2D* self, const Actor2DRecord* rec)
summary: Initialises a 2D actor from its placement record: resolves the model/anim record, stores position, size, model kind and the four u16 parameters, then attaches the sprite child.
evidence: Uses the same model-lookup chain as the named sibling 0x003A2760 (func_0066A7B8 -> 0062C388 -> 0062C3B0) and is called from the class factory at 0x003476E8 like the other Actor2D_* creators; the tail is a decompiler artefact of a never-returning call, not extra logic.

name: maybe_Field_InitObjectTable
summary: Allocates the field object-entry array, initialises each entry's shared parameter block and stores the table on the field (globals g_00206acc..g_00206ae0).
evidence: Only callees are Mem_AllocAligned_2 / Ui_Object_InitMemberPair / maybe_Field_InitSharedParams; no caller and no table stride survives, so 'object table' is still an inference from the field globals and the shared-parameter block it calls.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_InitChildB
summary: Creates a 0xAC-byte child scene object and copies four position/scale vectors into it from the global template at PTR_DAT_002F4374->f_130..0x13C. Same body shape as FUN_002B535C.
evidence: No new evidence: the '_DAT_00000064..0x70' writes are Ghidra alias artefacts, so the destination is really the new child; the class (scene node vs model part) is still unproven.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneNode_EnsureChild
summary: Lazily creates the node's 0x134-byte child scene object when f_13C is still null and copies the default vectors from g_002F56C0 into it.
evidence: The early-out on f_13C and the 0x134 allocation are clear, but nothing names the class; the 'Ensure' reading comes from the null guard, the 'scene node' part is still a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_SubWidgetConfig_Init
summary: Creates the first sub-widget (0x194 bytes) and copies a large global layout/config table of colours, rectangles and flags into its fields (+0x18..+0xC0).
evidence: Caller is now confirmed as maybe_Ui_InitFourSubWidgets (0x0027B508), which builds four equal sub-widgets - so 'sub-widget' is supported, but the copied block is not proven to be a config table (uniform copy pattern only).

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPartList_Init
summary: Allocates a 0xAC-byte list object with two 0x40-byte entries and copies the default 3-float triples from 0x003A3420/0x003A3430 into them; vtable 0x00767B54.
evidence: No caller at all, and the two-entry 0x40-stride array could be any small holder; the model-part reading is inherited from the neighbouring Gfx_ model code.

name: maybe_Ui_SubWidgetConfig_InitB
summary: Second sub-widget creator: allocates a 0xEC-byte widget, installs its vtables (0x0076A158 / 0x0076D2F8 / 0x0076D3D8) and copies a 0x50-word default configuration block into it.
evidence: Same construction pattern as 0x0038BF68 and 0x003A32D8 (0x0021C2DC + 0x00100050 with a 0x40 stride), so it belongs to the same family, but the class is not identified.

name: maybe_Gfx_SharedRenderState_Apply
summary: Uploads the shared 32-word render-state block at 0x623590 into the fixed GPU register window 0x20..0xA0 of a lazily created 300-byte state object (vtable slot +0x0C of three sibling classes).
evidence: The readable C is distorted (_DAT_ symbols and absolute-address writes), so the PICA200 register-window reading is best-effort; keep it low-confidence.

name: Ui_MessagePairWindow_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a message window that owns one message pair (vtable 0x007712EC, slot 4 = Ui_MessagePair_SetupPanels) and nine 0x18-byte message parts.
evidence: The installed vtable's own slots are now named (Ui_MessagePair_SetupPanels 0x44FBB4, Ui_Window_UpdateMessageArgs 0x44FD94) and the nine-element array uses ctor 0x6CF318 at stride 0x18 - that is a message-pair window, matching the previous guess.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitHandlerList4
summary: Child initialiser: stores the vtable, empties the two list links and builds the embedded listener object plus exactly four 0x18-byte handler entries (g_005D45FC).
evidence: Sibling entry 0x5D451C is the 4-byte-earlier variant that preloads the vtable and 0x5D6588 calls it; four entries is certain, the 'gimmick' class comes from the 0x5D46xx..0x5D51xx neighbourhood only.

name: maybe_Ui_ApplyLayoutConfig
signature: void Ui_ApplyLayoutConfig(Window* self, const u16* config)
summary: Applies a binary layout configuration to a window: allocates the child widgets and copies each placement record from the u16 config array.
evidence: Still only inferred: the body allocates with 0x00109DC8 and reads u16 records from arg2, but no named caller or layout-table reference confirms the 'layout config' reading.

name: Actor_ActionList_SortByPriority
summary: Replaces the holder's active action list and sorts it by the priority byte at +0x34 (decimation sort with gap 13); this is what keeps field/NPC action and animator lists ordered.
evidence: The sort key `*(u8*)(item+0x34)` and the 0x4EC4EC4F (divide-by-13) gap arithmetic are visible, and five named callers use it purely to install a list: Field_SetupNpcActionScript, Field_RegisterNpcActions, Field_RegisterActorActions, Ui_ActionWindow_CreateChildren, Ui_ActionPane_InitAnimators.

name: maybe_Party_GetMemberRecordBit1
summary: Six-instruction getter: reads the character id at member+0xC8, looks the character record up with func_0063F8F0(dataManager,id) and returns bit 1 of its flags byte (+4).
evidence: The old name was wrong: the body loads nothing but a flag bit, there is no model or equipment work. func_0063F8F0 turned out (asm 0x63F8F0) to be a bounded accessor into a 32-entry, 0x24-byte table holding character records; the bit's meaning is unknown, so the name states the mechanism.

name: maybe_Party_IsReserveMember
summary: Returns 1 when the party member's character record has bit 0 clear and bit 1 set, i.e. the character is not in the active party but is still usable; returns 0 otherwise.
evidence: The body is the same character-record flag read as 0x0062917C/0x0062923C, not an action filter. Callers pick menu rows / apply equipment previews for such characters, which fits 'reserve member', but that label is an inference from usage and stays below 0.5.

name: maybe_Gfx_ObjectDesc_CtorA
summary: Allocates a graphics object descriptor, installs the descriptor vtable (g_004143e4 = 0x76e04c) and runs the shared descriptor initialiser.
evidence: Single vtable literal plus one init call; the sibling at 0x004145D8 does the same with another vtable, so 'CtorA' stays a placeholder for an unidentified class.

name: maybe_Ui_ObjectDesc_InitSubObject
summary: Asks the shared object factory (0x00193D84) for a descriptor, replaces its vtable with 0x00776BE8 and stores the caller's value at +0x28; called when the equipment window loads its preview model.
evidence: Sole external caller is Ui_EquipWindow_LoadPreviewModel (0x3E7DD0), so the 'preview sub-object' context is solid, but the class of the descriptor is not.

name: maybe_Ui_ObjectRef_IsFirstVariant
summary: Returns 1 when the wrapper's link flag (+0x44) is set, the link at +0x24 is non-null and the record reached through it has variant 0; 87 callers use the 0/1 result to pick between two SE ids.
evidence: The asm-level predicate is certain (ldrb [r0+0x44]; [r0+0x24]; helper 0x629128 returns the sign-extended low byte of the halfword at record+0xC), but 'first variant' is still an interpretation of the value 0 - callers only show that it selects between SE 0xb and 0xc.

name: Gfx_SceneObject_DrawParts
signature: void Gfx_SceneObject_DrawParts(void* self, void* cmd, u32 ctx, u16* partIndex, void* color, u32* drawState)
summary: Draws the parts of a sized scene/overlay object: selects per-part state, binds texture state, writes the matrix/colour vertex-uniform blocks and emits the part quads honouring the clip/fade flags. Vtable method (PTRREF table 0x007828D8), no direct callers.
evidence: Twelve callees are now named (Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteMeshPartCommands, Gfx_MaterialState_WriteConstants, Gfx_MeshChunk_DrawPartList, Gfx_DrawRecord_WriteSubBuffers, ...), which pins this to the mesh-part draw path rather than to a sprite.

name: Snd_QueueCommandBuffer
signature: void Snd_QueueCommandBuffer(CommandBuffer* self, u32 size, u32 flags, int* out)
summary: Reserves `size` words in a command ring, links the new command node into the submit queue, bumps the sequence number and advances the write pointer (wrapping at the ring end).
evidence: Named neighbours (Os_QueueTryPop/Os_QueuePopBlocking, Sound_Stream_SubmitDmaCommand, Sound_Voice_SendBufferCommand) and 22 callers in the 0x0054xxxx stream/archive code confirm a ring-buffer command submit; the 'Snd_' prefix should be read as 'sound/stream command ring'.

name: maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve
signature: u32* maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve(u32* ring, u32 arg2, int count, u32* arg4, u32* arg5, u32* arg6)
summary: Looks for `count` contiguous free words in the same command ring used by Snd_QueueCommandBuffer and returns a pointer to them, tracking the ring's read/write positions across the wrap.
evidence: The old 'Gfx_FindCommandRoom' was wrong on subsystem: the ring helper it calls (func_0011C8E0, the Os_QueueTryPop of 0x0011B57C) and its caller 0x0010C1C8 belong to the sound/stream command ring. Ghidra gave up on most of the body (in_cr14/in_cr4 pseudo-registers), so the arithmetic is not trustworthy - damaged body, kept at 0.3.

name: maybe_Sound_Command_FreeQueued
signature: void maybe_Sound_Command_FreeQueued(OsQueue* queue, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Drains a sound command queue down to a given mark, releasing every queued command through 0x00548800 and signalling the consumer with 0x001166B4 via the queue object at queue+0xB4.
evidence: Only structural evidence: it walks with the Os_QueueTryPop helper and the same wake/commit call as 0x0011B57C, and the nodes come from the function immediately before the command executor 0x00548808. Called from both sound driver tick variants.

name: maybe_Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteVariant
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Scene_DrawSpriteVariant(GfxSceneSprite* self, u32 spriteId, u32 arg3, u32 flags)
summary: Fourth sprite submission variant: identical body to 0x2E58E0 but submits through 0x58E3F4 with self->f_14, the sprite id and a pointer to self->f_1C.
evidence: Same-body-as relationship is solid (only the submit helper differs), but which of the four sprite passes this is cannot be told from the callers, so the name stays generic.

name: maybe_Field_Action_MoveStep
summary: Per-frame movement step, the twin of maybe_Field_Action_UpdateMove (0x003028C0) without the blocked-state switch: integrates speed with the input stick, applies the collision-corrected delta and only plays the bump animation when the move is blocked.
evidence: Now that 0x003028C0 is named maybe_Field_Action_UpdateMove, the difference is explicit: the same analogue/dead-zone/vtable 0x30/0x34/0x38 sequence, but a blocked move only calls func_005E7848(actor,code,0) instead of switching the action state.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC(SpriteActor* self, float arg2, void* arg3, void* arg4, void* arg5)
summary: Variant child-object factory that also creates a row of up to eight animated sprites from a table of frame definitions, reusing the 0x328-byte sprite ctor and the func_003DFA44 flag registration.
evidence: Damaged body: Ghidra lost the registers (halt_baddata at 0x00336230, CONCAT chains), so only the caller set (field actors/effects, same as 0x00335A6C) is real; the signature beyond self is not.

name: Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTable
signature: void Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTable(FieldScene* scene, u32 table, u8* records, u32 count, int mode, u8 flags, int layer, u8 arg8)
summary: Walks a scene object table (1431-line body) and spawns each record's actor/sprite/model through the field spawn helpers, including effect and collision objects; sole caller is the object-table initialiser at 0x0033A140.
evidence: Named callees now cover the whole spawn path (Field_SpawnObjectVariant, Field_Scene_AddActorObject, Field_SceneObject_CopyRecord, Container_TreeMap_InsertOrFindB) and the single caller fills the table; that is exactly a table-driven object spawner. The damaged-body flag does not apply: asm/text/text_00300048.s line 60315 shows the function as intact ARM - a counted loop over work+0x24A08 (count +0x84, id array +0x80, byte array +0xA8) calling the spawn helper 0x0033DEC4 - so the unaff_ registers are only Ghidra's lost register recovery, not broken control flow.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildD
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildD(SpriteActor* self, void* tmpl, void* params, u32 arg4, int arg5)
summary: Largest variant of the sprite-child factory: allocates and initialises sprite rows with the 0x328-byte ctor, registers them with the parent and updates a flag through func_003DFA44.
evidence: Control flow is only partially recovered (CONCAT artefacts, two 0x328 allocations) and the class comes from the caller set; same family as 0x00335A6C/0x00336054.

name: Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateMain
summary: Main update of the field actor-action sequence player: runs the current 100-byte action entry, plays its SE/animation, waits for the actor and then advances to the next entry or ends the sequence (ten switch cases on the state word at self[0x882]).
evidence: Named helpers now describe the loop: Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty, Field_ActorActionSeq_RunSteps, FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine, Sound_PlaySeById, BattleScene_SyncUnitModels - and the per-entry layout (id at +0x2A, actor index at +0x166/0x168) matches the append/begin siblings 0x003C123C and 0x003C1A00.

name: Party_IsMemberActive
summary: Returns bit 0 of the character record found for the member's id at +0xC8 through func_0063F8F0(dataManager,id) - i.e. whether the character currently belongs to the active party.
evidence: Two named callers settle the meaning: Item_FindInInventory (0x00254C20) only searches the inventory of members where this is non-zero, and Party_Status_RebuildRows (0x0023C588) shows or hides the member row from the same result. Party_CountAliveMembers counts the same bit.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_OpenSceneField
summary: Scene handler for the field variant (no fixed slot id): at state 9 it resets the render mode, configures the camera from the scene descriptor, binds the field scene object ids and pushes the message/fade descriptor.
evidence: Its own body is now surrounded by named Ui_SceneFlow_* helpers (AdvanceState, ApplyWindowSetup, CanOpenScene, IsIdle, LoadWorldMapModels), so the Ui_SceneFlow prefix is solid, but 'field variant' still rests on the absence of a slot id.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_Release2dCommonPack
summary: Counterpart of the 2dcmn.pack loader: releases the item list, message window, 2D screen and scene system, unloads the shared 2dcmn.pack when it is still mounted and resets the layer render modes.
evidence: Named callees (Gfx_Effect2D_ReleasePack, Pack_HandleTable_ReleaseObjects, Ui_SceneFlow_SetLayerVisible, Field_Level_ResetRuntime) plus the pack-manager test 0x006456A4(pack,5) confirm the 2dcmn.pack release path; callers 0x0019F908 and 0x001A04A4.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_Apply2dCommonPack
summary: Loads/keeps the shared 2dcmn.pack set for the current scene mode: shows the matching UI layer (1/2/3/4) and, when the pack is not loaded in this mode, asks the pack manager to load '2dcmn.pack', binds it to the 2D screen and runs the scene continuation.
evidence: The pooled string '2dcmn.pack' at 0x001A275C is the direct evidence, and the named callees (Gfx_Effect2D_LoadCommonPack, Pack_HandleTable_Acquire, Fs_NamedObject_LoadAndAdd) show the load path; sole caller 0x001A04A4.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_AdvanceState
summary: Advances a message-window state machine from states 9/10/11 (name plate / page / close); on other states it increments f_1D, restamps the timer and notifies the text manager (0x626050).
evidence: Switch values and the timer restamp are clear, but the Ui_SceneFlow_* neighbours use the same state values, so whether this drives a message window or the scene flow itself is unresolved.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetColorByState
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_SetColorByState(u32 handle, const char* record)
summary: Selects a colour index from a state record (bytes 3/4/0/1) and applies palette entry 4 or 7 to the widget through func_0064553C after looking its name up with 0x0056F768.
evidence: Only the call sequence is known (func_001068AC + func_0064553C(handle,colour,7 or 4)); which record supplies the state is not identifiable.

name: maybe_Script_SetBookCommandParams
summary: Publishes four script parameters to the running .cnut script while the script object is active (guarded by f_94), using the four pooled names g_002555E4..g_002555F0.
evidence: Same shape as the named 0x00253EA0 parameter setter and called from 0x001A04A4/0x00624958, but the 'book' screen attribution comes only from the four pooled strings.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_Type6
signature: void maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_Type6(u32 scene, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Queues a layout/format request of type 6 for the scene: builds the stack argument with the low byte forced to 6 and tail-calls 0x6D9730.
evidence: Type byte 6 and the tail call are certain; the sibling entries (0x2D6BB0 type 4 -> 0x6DDFA4, 0x2D6C7C type 5 -> 0x6E0B28) show this is one of a family of request wrappers, but what the type selects is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_Type4
signature: void maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_Type4(u32 scene, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Queues a layout/format request of type 4 for the scene (type byte 4 in the stack argument, tail-call 0x6DDFA4); called from Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState.
evidence: Type byte and tail target verified; the request family is only inferred from the three siblings.

name: maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_Type5
signature: void maybe_Ui_LayoutRequest_Type5(u32 scene, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Queues a layout/format request of type 5 for the scene (type byte 5, tail-call 0x6E0B28); called from Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState.
evidence: Type byte and tail target verified; same unresolved family as 0x2D6B68/0x2D6BB0.

name: Ui_IsCloseableDefaultTrue
summary: Virtual default implementation that always returns 1, used by UI objects that are always closeable; the scene-flow state machine uses the result as its 'may close' decision.
evidence: The body really is `return 1` and the only caller (Ui_SceneFlow_AdvanceState) branches on it as a close permission, so the predicate name is not a dropped-return artefact (it returns a value).

name: Ui_GetSceneTransitionManager
summary: Lazily creates the 0x28-byte scene-transition/state singleton (class table 0x006F1DF4) and returns it through the out slot.
evidence: Same lazy-singleton template as the now-named siblings 0x6F1DF8/0x6F1EEC/0x6F202C/0x6F245C, and callers are the scene-flow state machine (where local->f_c blocks the transition), message-window close paths and the debug menu.

name: maybe_FieldParty_ApplyAttachmentSlots
summary: Spawns the attachments/effects described by a parameter block for one or two actors: id/duration pairs pass through 0x00398744/0x0039881C and func_001FCF80, plus a UI-window notification branch.
evidence: The 0x20-record / 0x7c-byte table at group+0x164 (filled by func_001FCF80) and the id sources at params +0xa/+6/+0x16 are visible, but 'attachment slots' is still a reading of that table.

name: maybe_Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel
signature: void maybe_Menu_TalkParty_CreatePanel(void* self, u32 index, u32 arg3)
summary: Creates (or tears down) one talk-party sub-panel by index, choosing the concrete class per index (text, choice, face, ...) and destroying the old slot first.
evidence: The literal 'talk_party.bxon' and the ~30 named UI ctors (Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor, Ui_MessageSelectWindow_Ctor, ...) in the switch are the evidence; the per-index class mapping is not decoded.

name: Event_ResetState
summary: Resets the event/cutscene runtime: clears both completion flags, clears the pending script contexts, drains the queued command list, runs the four sub-system resets and marks the state idle.
evidence: The field writes (f_3D8/f_3D9=0, f_428/f_429=0xFF), the 0x14-byte command-vector drain and the sub-reset calls 0x00255140/0x00253264/0x00162E98/0x0025370C are all visible; 'ResetState' is the plain description, no caller needed.

name: maybe_Ui_TextLineCache_InitAndReturn
summary: Expression-form initialiser of the text line cache: clears the three 0x180-byte blocks at self+{0,0x180,0x300} and zeroes f_480..f_495, then returns self.
evidence: Identical to 0x00398ADC except for returning the pointer; the 'text line cache' label comes from that sibling's neighbourhood, not from the body.

name: maybe_Ui_LargeStateObjectCtor
signature: void maybe_Ui_LargeStateObjectCtor(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Constructor for a ~13 KB state object: installs a vtable and clears a long run of fields with -1/0xFFFF sentinels (offsets 0xC91..0xCA6); no string or caller identifies the owning screen.
evidence: Only base-object create (0x0031EECC, now Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache) and the reset helper 0x001FF200 are identifiable; the owning screen is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_ScreenCtor_vt777B60
summary: Constructor of a Ui object class that also creates its render/transition child: Ui_Screen_CtorWithTextCache then 0x002689E8, with vtable 0x777B60 and two zeroed defaults.
evidence: Called from the scene factory 0x006C1E68; the vtable literal is the only class identifier, hence the address in the name instead of an invented class name.

name: maybe_Battle_ActorAction_Sequence
signature: u32* maybe_Battle_ActorAction_Sequence(void* self, void* action, void* ctx, void* out)
summary: Long multi-stage battle actor action: plays the record's SE cues (offsets 0x6/0x10/0x12), moves the actor toward its target, spawns popups/effects per record id and returns a pointer into the action data.
evidence: Named callees (Sound_PlaySeById, FieldParty_MoveActorTowardTarget, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnFromTable, Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnForModelActors) confirm a scripted battle action, but the state machine is too large to pin the exact stage.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelAttach_SetLocatorPairFromActor
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelAttach_SetLocatorPairFromActor(void* self, void* actor, u32 arg3)
summary: Resolves the actor record through 0x0063FD24, clears the +0x54/+0x55 flags and caches the record's two 16-bit locator ids (f_138/f_12E) in the attachment object.
evidence: Callers are all named battle-pose/motion code (Battle_ActorAction_UpdatePose/_UpdateMotion/_SpawnImpactEffects, Monster_Model_UpdateWeaponLocators) and 0x0063FD24 is the same action-row accessor used to read locator-set ids, so 'locator pair' is well supported - but the exact slot semantics in this attachment object are not.

name: maybe_Battle_ComposeMessageText
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_ComposeMessageText(void* ctx, void* arg2, void* arg3)
summary: Builds one formatted battle message: initialises the 0x3c0-byte text builder, sets the speaker from the name entry, formats via 0x00459FE0 and reports whether anything usable was produced.
evidence: The builder chain (Text_LayoutState_Init, Text_SetFormatArgsFromPlayerData, Text_Layout_Init) is named now, but 'battle' is inferred from the caller set only.

name: maybe_Ui_List_BuildRows
signature: void maybe_Ui_List_BuildRows(void* self, void* entries, u32 count)
summary: Builds up to four list rows: allocates a 0x21C-byte row block, formats the labels through 0x63638C/0x6364F4, copies the twelve row fields and marks the selected row from the entry flags.
evidence: ~24 UI list/table callers and the 0x21C/4-iteration structure support 'build rows', but the class of list (window list vs table) is not identified.

name: maybe_Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableThumb
signature: void maybe_Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableThumb(FieldScene* scene, u8* records, u32 count)
summary: Thumb-mode twin of the scene-table spawner at 0x00336BE4 (the ROM contains ARM and Thumb copies of the routine): spawns actors, sprites and effects from a record table.
evidence: Callee set matches 0x00336BE4 (Field_Scene_AddActorObject, Field_SceneObject_SpawnFromRecord, Model_Equip_UpdateActorEquipment) and the entry is flagged Thumb; no callers.

name: maybe_Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableB
signature: void maybe_Field_Scene_SpawnObjectsFromTableB(FieldScene* scene, u8* records, u32 count)
summary: Alternate record-table spawner used by the big scene loader: creates field actors with model/portrait/effect setup and NPC collision.
evidence: Sole caller 0x0033AD44 plus the 'NPC_Collision' string and Field_SpawnObjectRecordB/C calls; the A/B distinction from the other two spawners is only caller-based.

name: maybe_Field_Scene_AddObjectEntryC
signature: void maybe_Field_Scene_AddObjectEntryC(FieldScene* scene, u32 layer, void* data)
summary: Scene-object record factory: creates a 0x3B4-byte record, gives it a unique id from the global counter 0x7A316C and links it into the per-layer list at scene+0x128+layer*0xC.
evidence: Shape identical to the three named siblings 0x6C2B18/0x6C2BD4/0x6C2D4C (alloc + ctor + virtual slot +0xC + id + list link), so the operation is certain; the trailing letter still just distinguishes four same-shaped creators.

name: maybe_Battle_PushDamageActionEntry
signature: void maybe_Battle_PushDamageActionEntry(void* self, void* action, u32 slot, u32 value)
summary: Variant of the battle action-entry push used for actions that show damage/heal numbers: measures the text run, clears and fills the current action slot, builds the actor action sequence and spawns the number popups.
evidence: The same f_877*0x19 slot arithmetic as 0x426E44 plus Text_MeasureTextRun and Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnNumberList show the damage-number path, but the exact entry kind is inferred.

name: Gfx_CommandNode_InitSixSlots
summary: Default-constructs six 0x18-byte GPU state nodes in place (element ctor 0x5096B8); companion of 0x509638, which builds the same nodes as a chain.
evidence: Exactly six std_ConstructArray elements of 0x18 bytes with ctor 0x5096B8, and 27 callers, all named Gfx_ModelInstance draw/bind passes that also use the chain builder 0x509638.

name: Ui_TextLayout_BuildRows
summary: Master layout pass of a window content block: measures every entry of the three content lists, creates the candidate slots and fills the 0x14-byte row records that the mode dispatcher then sorts and trims.
evidence: Called once at the top of the now-named Ui_TextLayout mode dispatcher (0x0026DF1C), which then sorts the 16 slots with comparator 0x00270808; every callee is a named Ui_TextLayout_* measurement helper. The damaged-body flag does not apply: asm/text/text_00240048.s line 55611 shows an intact ARM prologue (0x2C0-byte frame, vpush d8) and a real loop, so the unaff_ registers in the readable C are Ghidra register-recovery noise.

name: Field_CreateRenderObject
signature: int Field_CreateRenderObject(FieldOwner* owner, u32 charaId, int variant, int mode)

Returns the object's handle word.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_FinishActorMessage
summary: Single-state step of the battle party panel that closes one actor's message: posts the model-actor popup entry for the actor id at self+0x497 (state 0x274B) and, when Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty returns, sets the battle-work byte +0x424B to 1, clears the actor's UI flag and ends the step (-2 / state 0x2758).

Sibling method of Battle_Ui_UpdatePartyPanel in vtable 0x00774680; state ids 0x274B/0x2758 sit in the same state family as the message stepper's 0x27AE/0x27BA.

name: maybe_Battle_CutsceneObject_InitFromParams
signature: void maybe_Battle_CutsceneObject_InitFromParams(BattleCutscene* self, u32 id, int arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, ... arg6)
summary: Battle cut-scene part builder. The readable first block (entry 0x003615A8) walks the part table of the '.btcs' cut-scene resource, creates one sprite actor per part with Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, builds its Anim_Instance_CtorSprite with the 's_%s.btcs'-derived name, sets the model size and registers the child with Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChild. evidence: Now-named neighbours confirm the readable half is part construction: Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable, Anim_Instance_CtorSprite, Field_SceneObject_SetModelSize, Gfx_ModelInstance_InitWithTransform, Model_Node_ComputeWorldMatrix, std__Rb_tree_insert_and_rebalance. But the body is badly damaged (unaff_r4/r5/r6/r7/r9, in_r12, argNN pseudo-globals, and blocks at 0x003613EC-0x003610FC that lie *below* the entry address), so the Ghidra signature and the 'FromParams' wording cannot be verified - name and confidence stay an honest maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TextLayout_FillSlotsByMode

evidence: Seven named layout-mode callers (e.g. func_00269F64 calls it with mode 1) and the 16-slot qsort are visible; which source each mode selects is not decoded.

name: Ui_TextLayout_LayoutMode3
summary: Layout strategy 3: the widest multi-line mode (0xA1C bytes) - it fits characters with fixed-point measurements and appends per-character runs for the wrapping pass.
evidence: It is the case-3 branch of the mode dispatchers, uses the 0.01f/1/65536f constants at 0x00276E44/0x00276E48 and the now-named run appenders (Ui_TextLayout_BuildElementTable, Ui_TextLayout_AppendBestCandidateAllSources, Ui_TextLayout_CheckSlotsFit).

name: Ui_TextLayout_LayoutMode7
summary: Layout strategy 7: clears the record buffer, then tries the single-line fit and the all-sources pass with category 7 (used by the multi-line message styles).
evidence: The 0x9BC0 clear, the qsort comparator pair 0x00276124/0x00276128 and the explicit category 7 argument to func_00272044 identify the mode; callers 0x0026F540 and 0x002773B8.

name: Ui_TextLayout_LayoutMode8
summary: Layout strategy 8: single-line fit first, then the all-sources candidate pass with category 8 (the 'short label' style), then the filtered fallback.
evidence: Explicit category 8 argument to func_00272044, its own qsort pair 0x00277A18/0x00277A1C and the same two callers as mode 7.

name: Ui_TextLayout_AppendControlElement
summary: Appends a fixed four-byte control/separator descriptor {2, variant, 0, 0} to the layout when the current element id resolves to a record; the variant becomes 2 or 3 for element kinds 0x13/0x0F without a record.
evidence: The descriptor bytes (local_28=2, local_27=1/2/3) passed to the append routine 0x0026D9F0, which reads bytes [1] and [3], and the 0xFFFF 'no record' path are explicit; Ui_TextLayout_* neighbours name the consumer.

name: Ui_TextLayout_ProcessPendingRequest
summary: Second half of the two-step layout request: clears the context slots, re-runs the chosen mode and finally hands the selected element to the current-actor layout.
evidence: Sole caller 0x00270CCC, and the body calls the whole now-named mode family (Ui_TextLayout_LayoutMode0/1/2/4, GatherElementList, BuildElementTable) after zeroing ctx[8..10].

name: Ui_ResolveObjectHandle
summary: Resolves the object handle at self->f_26C through the 2D object table and stores the found object in self->f_270; called from 29 field/UI update paths.
evidence: The standard handle validation (>>0xB against the table word, vtable-chain compare with 0x7C4360) plus 0x62B3E4(ctx->f_54, self->f_26C, 0) and the 29 callers make this a plain handle resolver.
